title: Complete copy and rewind
statement: Let $L>0$, let a machine have $L+1$ work tapes, and let $q_c,q_r,q_a$ be states and $f$ a Boolean map. Suppose that in state $q_c$ the machine reads the last tape: on a symbol $b$ it writes $f(b)$ on tape zero, blanks the last tape, moves both heads right, and remains in $q_c$; on a blank it makes no writes, moves both heads left, and enters $q_r$. Suppose that in state $q_r$ it reads tape zero: on a symbol it makes no writes, moves both heads left, and remains in $q_r$; on a blank it makes no writes, moves both heads right, and enters $q_a$. For words $\mathit{old}$ and $v$ with $|\mathit{old}|\le |v|$, starting with the two heads at zero, tape zero storing $\mathit{old}$, and the last tape storing $v$, after $2|v|+2$ steps the machine is in state $q_a$, tape zero stores the word obtained by applying $f$ to each symbol of $v$, the last tape is blank, and both heads are at zero.
hypotheses_covered: The specified transition rule in state $q_c$ for a symbol on the last tape
The specified transition rule in state $q_c$ for a blank on the last tape
The specified transition rule in state $q_r$ for a symbol on tape zero
The specified transition rule in state $q_r$ for a blank on tape zero
replaced:
For a machine with copy and rewind states as in the two preceding scans: if the
captured word $v$ is at least as long as the old tape-zero word, then from a
two-ended configuration with both heads at zero, exactly $2|v| + 2$ steps replace
tape zero entirely by $f$ mapped over $v$, blank the capture tape, and return
both heads to zero in the arrival state.
